disclaimer: General wellness information, not medical advice. Evidence on meal frequency is mixed; athlete-derived fueling guidance is applied to strenuous hikes.

rules.notes: Eat three planned meals (don't skip breakfast or lunch) plus one snack. The AHA scientific statement (St-Onge 2017) reports that skipping breakfast and irregular meals are associated with worse cardiometabolic markers, but this evidence is mostly observational, and trials on meal frequency are mixed. For someone who tends to undereat, regular planned meals are a practical way to reach energy and protein needs (DGA 2025-2030: protein at every meal; 1.2-1.6 g/kg/day = ~110-145 g/day, i.e. roughly 30-40 g per meal over 3 meals plus a snack). No trial-based minimum or maximum gap between meals exists for the general population, so both are null. Intermittent fasting / time-restricted eating is NOT recommended here: trials show no added weight or metabolic benefit over regular calorie-matched eating in most people (Lowe 2020; Liu 2022), and it works against the goal of eating enough.

rules.notes: Strenuous hikes >1 h: eat a carbohydrate-containing meal 1-4 h before (ACSM 2016: 1-4 g carbohydrate/kg, i.e. ~90-360 g for 90.7 kg). During activity lasting 1-2.5 h aim for 30-60 g carbohydrate per hour (up to 90 g/h for >2.5 h), so maxHoursBetween = 1 applies to eating occasions DURING the hike (small snacks hourly: e.g. dried fruit, banana, trail mix, PB on whole-grain crackers). After: a meal/snack with carbohydrate and ~0.25-0.3 g/kg protein (~23-27 g) (ACSM 2016; ISSN 2017). Spreading protein every ~3-4 h is an ISSN recommendation from athlete studies (moderate evidence in athletes, limited for general adults). The 'snacksPerDay' is null because it depends on duration and intensity. Evidence base is mainly from athletes; adapt to hike length and how you feel.

rules.notes: Chrononutrition: some small trials suggest earlier eating windows improve insulin sensitivity (Sutton 2018: 8 men with prediabetes, 5 weeks), but this is preliminary (limited evidence) and is not a recommendation here. Perishable packed foods should not sit unrefrigerated for >2 h (>1 h above 90°F) per USDA FSIS — pack a cooler/ice pack or choose 'no-cooler' snacks on field days.

hydration.notes: National Academies Adequate Intake for men 19+: 3.7 L/day TOTAL water (beverages + food moisture), of which ~3.0 L (about 13 cups) from beverages. This is an Adequate Intake (population median), not a precise requirement; needs rise with heat and activity. Bach-Faig 2011 suggests 1.5-2 L/day of water as the main drink.

hydration.notes: Pre-hydrate ~5-7 ml/kg at least 4 h before exercise = 454-635 ml for 90.7 kg (ACSM 2007; ACSM 2016). Add 3-5 ml/kg ~2 h before if no urine or it is dark.

hydration.notes: About 0.4-0.8 L per hour during exercise, adjusted for heat, terrain and individual sweat rate (ACSM 2016). Goal: avoid losing >2% of body weight (~1.8 kg for 90.7 kg) without over-drinking (over-drinking beyond sweat losses risks hyponatremia). A single number is not supported because sweat rates vary widely; weigh yourself before/after hikes to learn your rate. For long or very sweaty hikes, drinks/foods containing sodium help (ACSM 2007 suggests ~20-30 mEq/L sodium in fluids for prolonged exercise); DGA 2025-2030 notes highly active people may need more than 2,300 mg sodium/day.
